Among the eliminated suspects was a 31-year-old man who was arrested the day of the offense and later deported.

Ireland secured a 4-1 victory over Poland in a must-win match of the World League 3 quarter-finals, with goals by McKee (twice), Eugene Magee, and O'Donoghue. Craig Fulton, Ireland coach, highlighted strong team play and the team's success in capturing the ball in critical areas, even though they left several more scoring opportunities. The winners, Ireland, will advance to the semi-finals on Saturday, facing Wales. France and Scotland will compete in the other semi-final at the same venue.

Philip Craig, a 38-year-old from Leeds, was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum of 25 years for the stabbing murder of Christopher Laskaris, a 24-year-old man with Asperger's Syndrome and bi-polar disorder, in Leeds in November. Craig had pleaded guilty to burglary at a previous hearing and was also sentenced to three years, to be served concurrently. The court noted that Craig took advantage of Laskaris' vulnerabilities, exploiting him for drugs and stealing his possessions after his death.

The Metropolitan Police has closed its reinvestigation into the 2010 death of Kester David, a man believed to have been killed for working as a police informant, acknowledging previous failings in their initial investigation, including not checking CCTV or interviewing witnesses promptly. Despite several appeals, no arrests have been made in connection with his death.

In 2015, football had the highest total attendance with 43.4 million, followed by three horse racing events in the top 10. Rugby union improved with the Rugby World Cup, reaching 7.5 million. Notably, Wimbledon was the most attended individual event with just under half a million spectators, while the British Grand Prix had the highest attendance per event day. Horseracing was also a popular spectator sport, expected to reach a record 6.2 million in 2015. The article also mentions the inclusion of two new events, MotoGP's British Grand Prix and the Badminton Horse Trials, in the top 10 best-attended sporting events of 2015.

Beyoncé had the highest-grossing year of her career in 2013-2014, earning an estimated $105 million, followed by Taylor Swift at $64 million, Pink at $52 million, Rihanna at $48 million, and Katy Perry at $40 million, according to Forbes, based on income from touring, record sales, publishing, merchandise sales, endorsements, and other ventures. Additional artists mentioned include Madonna, Nicki Minaj, and Alicia Keys.

The Scottish National Party claims it has more MP support than Labour Leader Jeremy Corbyn, but Speaker John Bercow recognizes Labour as the official opposition due to its larger number of MPs, despite Corbyn losing a vote of no confidence and his shadow cabinet resigning in numbers.

The villagers of Crickhowell successfully launched a bid to buy The Corn Exchange and prevent its conversion into a supermarket, with plans to transform the building into independent shops with flats above, under the management of a new company called Corn Exchange Crickhowell Ltd.

RIT Capital will not make a formal bid for Alliance Trust, which is engaging in a strategic review that could result in a sale, outsourcing investment, or a deal with RIT, and has taken the company out of the UK's formal takeover and merger procedures.

Alexis Scott, 39, a former Police Community Support Officer, was convicted for tricking long-haul airline passengers into thinking they had excess cash on them during flights in April 2013. She was sentenced to time in prison, splitting her from her young daughter, due to the severity of the predatory crime that exploited victims' panic and affected international trust in the UK.

Educational platform TrueTube has received three award nominations for its drama and learning categories, notably for the films Refugee and Katie. Horrible Histories, on the other hand, earned three nominations for its special Shakespeare-themed episode, including comedy, writing, and best performer for actor Tom Stourton. Various other programs, including Cartoon Network's The Amazing World of Gumball, CBBC's Hetty Feather, and The Dog Ate my Homework, have also received multiple nominations. The 2019 Bafta Children's Awards will take place on November 20 at the Roundhouse in London, with various movie, game, and interactive categories being acknowledged.

Lady Mary Soames, the last surviving child of Sir Winston Churchill, bequeathed most of her collection of Churchill's artworks, including "Coast Scene near Cannes" and "View From a Bathing Hut at the Miami Surf Club," to the National Trust, Houses of Parliament, and Churchill War Rooms, with the paintings being accepted in lieu of inheritance tax. The collection also includes works by Sir John Lavery and the Aly Khan Gold Cup, won by Churchill's horse, High Hat. The 50th anniversary of Churchill's death was recently commemorated, and the paintings are being displayed in locations that influenced his life, such as Chartwell and Whitehall, providing insights into Churchill as an artist and a political leader.

An ex-investigator from the ombudsman's office was arrested for alleged theft of sensitive security documents containing information potentially endangering lives. This has raised concerns among the police federation, officials, and a parliament member regarding the ombudsman's office's handling of sensitive material and the need for independence in investigations. The police have begun a criminal investigation and temporarily halted the release of further sensitive materials to the ombudsman's office while they review security protocols.

Phyllis Schlafly, a conservative advocate and outspoken opponent of feminism, abortion, and the Equal Rights Amendment, helped shape Republican politics, particularly in the 1970s, and was credited with creating a political climate that assisted Ronald Reagan's rise to the presidency. She publicly endorsed Donald Trump and her death was celebrated as that of an iconic American leader who deeply loved her family and her country.

Twenty-three-year-old rugby player called Morgan is leaving Bristol at the end of the season to continue his career in Wales with Newport Gwent Dragons. He cites personal development and an opportunity to test himself at a higher level as reasons for the move. Morgan, who can play at full-back or fly-half, was previously with Ospreys, but limited game time there led to his transfer to Bristol. His new coach, Danny Wilson, expects him to play predominantly at full-back due to his speed and footwork, similar to Matthew, another player on their roster.

The article details the trial of two people smugglers, Mufawaka Alabash and Asem Alfrhad, charged with the death of Syrian toddler Alan Kurdi, who became a symbol of the refugee crisis. Despite being found guilty of people smuggling, they were acquitted of causing death through deliberate negligence. Alan's family, including his brother Galib and mother Rihan, also lost their lives attempting the same crossing. The discussion revolves around the ongoing migration crisis and potential solutions, such as talks between European Council President Donald Tusk and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, which include the idea of "shipping back" migrants arriving in Greece from Turkey.

Former Milan station chief Robert Lady, convicted in absentia for his involvement in the abduction and "extraordinary rendition" of Egyptian cleric Abu Omar, who was allegedly tortured, was released and boarded a US-bound flight according to American officials, after being arrested near Panama's border with Costa Rica. The Milan trial was the first involving the CIA's practice of transferring suspects to countries where torture is permitted, which has been condemned by human rights groups as a violation of international agreements.

The article reports that during January 2017, Edinburgh Airport experienced a significant 11.7% year-on-year increase in passenger traffic, most notably in international flights, due to the launching of 27 international services in 2016. Glasgow Airport reported an 8.4% rise, with strong demand for routes to Toronto, New York, Dubai, and within the EU. Aberdeen International Airport, on the other hand, saw its lowest decline in passenger numbers in almost two years, with a modest 1.7% drop, despite a 7% decrease in helicopter traffic.

The most-watched video on YouTube, Gangnam Style by Psy, has surpassed the previous view limit of 2.147 billion views, prompting YouTube to update its counter system to a 64-bit integer with a new maximum view limit of 9.22 quintillion views.

England, despite a rocky start with losses to West Indies and close calls against Afghanistan (57/6), aim to put their best performance together in the upcoming match against Sri Lanka to secure a semi-final spot in the World Twenty20. The struggling middle-order of the defending champions Sri Lanka, who lost their opener to the West Indies but recovered against Afghanistan, will be the next challenge for England. Alex Hales' return to the team is expected after recovering from injury.

Inrix Roadway Analytics reports that Edinburgh and Glasgow rank second and third respectively among Britain's most congested cities, with Edinburgh's traffic jams predicted to cost £2.8bn over the next decade, Glasgow's £2.3bn, and nationwide congestion hovers at a potential £61.8bn loss by 2025 if unchecked. London ranks as Europe's most congested city with the most traffic "pinch points," according to the firm's broader survey of 123 European cities.

In the 44th minute of a friendly, a deflected shot by Norway's Nordtveit off Sammy Clingan's heel beat keeper Lee Camp to give Norway a late first-half lead. Northern Ireland struggled to find a response, and Elyounoussi, Ruud, and another substitute extended Norway's lead over the remaining minutes. Northern Ireland's impressive start yielded few results, as they won just one of their last 14 friendlies.

Brussels remains on high alert as France continues an international manhunt for Salah Abdeslam, a suspect in the Paris attacks, and issues an arrest warrant for another individual, Mohamed Abrini, who allegedly drove a car with Abdeslam two days before the Paris attacks. The authorities have identified two other suspects and fear potential Paris-style attacks. The leaders of France and the US have renewed their commitment to eliminate IS.

There were multiple fatal explosions in Zaventem Airport and Maalbeek metro station in Brussels on March 22, causing numerous casualties, prompting national mourning, and increasing global security measures with potential links to previous attacks in Paris in 2015.

Sheffield City Council's Green Party councillor, Alison Teal, faces potential legal action for her involvement in protests against the city's tree felling program; the council asserts that the removal of street trees is lawful and necessary, having faced months of disruption by a handful of protesters, with works continuing to be disrupted despite previous warnings.

In New Zealand, about 416 whales have stranded themselves at Farewell Spit, South Island, resulting in almost 300 fatalities, making it one of the worst such incidents nationwide. Locals and conservation department staff formed a human chain to refloat the survivors, while experts continue to investigate the cause of whale strandings, which can occur due to a variety of factors including age, sickness, injury, navigational errors, and attracting other pod members due to distress signals. The incident highlights New Zealand's high stranding rate for marine mammals, with approximately 300 dolphins and whales found on beaches each year, with many incidents occurring at Farewell Spit.

Experienced prop forward Brian Mujati, with a history of playing at high levels in Super Rugby, Top 14, and Premiership, has been signed by Ospreys to provide injury cover for their current tight heads, Dmitri Arhip and Ma'afu Fia, particularly as the season progresses and the Challenge Cup quarter-final in April approaches. Coach Steve Tandy believes Mujati will add valuable experience to the squad and address the critical position of only having two fit tight heads in the team, given Rhodri Jones' potential Wales duty during the Six Nations.

The Gwynedd council has decided to proceed with establishing a new Church in Wales campus at Ysgol y Berwyn in Bala, despite opposition from community members, with the merging of two local schools and the involvement of multiple religious and non-religious individuals on the shadow governing body.

Oxfordshire County Council's plan to consolidate all services under one organization could save £100m over five years, but five district councils prefer three councils, sparking a disagreement over devolution plans. District councils advocate for an elected mayor to receive more funding from the government, while the county council argues the proposal is necessary to avoid further cuts to local services. Residents are currently being consulted on the proposal ahead of a county council cabinet decision on March 14.

Edinburgh Rugby, led by Dickinson, aims to win the remaining five matches in a tough run-in to have a shot at playoffs or the top six, starting with a challenging away game against Newport Gwent Dragons and continue with Zebre, Leinster, Munster, and Cardiff Blues. Edward aims to eliminate errors and finish opportunities to improve their performances, following recent losses in five out of six games under their coach, Solomons.

The Northern Ireland Bat Group, led by Karen Healy, is caring for an unprecedented number of grounded, malnourished, and injured young bats. Volunteers are hand-raising and nursing these bats back to health before releasing them back into the wild, with a pre-release assessment including checking their flying ability and weight. They hope to educate the public about the importance of bats, which have a significant positive impact on the economy due to their pest control abilities.

The Supreme Court, in its second week of oral arguments since the death of Justice Antonin Scalia, is considering placing new limits on the federal law banning people convicted of domestic violence from owning guns. Justice Thomas broke his long silence at the court, questioning a lawyer about whether any law violation suspends a person's constitutional rights.

British travel company Responsible Travel, after watching a BBC programme, decides to remove half a dozen trips involving zoos from their offerings of 3,500 tours. The firm's boss, Justin Francis, argues most animals in zoos are not endangered and few examples exist of endangered species being successfully reintroduced after captivity. This decision received support from the Born Free Foundation, with president Will Travers praising the move towards reducing animal exploitation in zoos worldwide.

A child of primary school age has been found deceased at a home in Faringdon, leading to a 40-year-old woman's arrest on suspicion of murder. The community has been advised to seek reassurance from local police. Police tape and increased police presence remain at the scene, and anyone with relevant information is asked to call the police.

A British suspect, known as BM, is accused of breaching Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures (TPIm) by failing to contact a monitoring company and report to a police station twice in January, which, if confirmed, would be the first alleged violation of TPIm. The defendant was granted bail pending a plea and case management hearing in July, with the trial date yet to be set. The Home Office declined to comment on the case, while the opposition party has criticized TPIm for weakening public protection against terrorism.

Qualcomm, the world's largest supplier of smartphone chips, agreed to China's largest corporate fine, lowering its royalty rates on patents used in China's mobile phone market. This move is expected to benefit Chinese smartphone makers Xiaomi and Huawei. Qualcomm sees a positive outlook for its business in China, generating about half of its global revenue from the country.

Michelle Mellotte, 61, has been barred from practicing as a doctor in the UK, following a police investigation and medical tribunal, for fraudulently obtaining £10,000 from an Alzheimer's patient in 2010, using her professional role, and putting patients at risk, bringing disrepute to the profession, and breaching fundamental tenets of her role.

A man, aged between 30 and 49, and nearly 6 feet tall, was found deceased near the M54 motorway in Shropshire, England, wearing specific clothing from 2007-2008. The cause of death remains unknown, and police continue to investigate whether this man may have been a victim of a crime. The remains are believed to have been undiscovered for up to three years.

The surprise discovery in Avebury, a 30m wide site known for its colossal stone circle, includes a "stone square circle" that is thought to be one of the site's earliest structures. This uncovered megalithic square, which encloses the obelisk, could potentially be a commemoration of the first people's ancestral house in Avebury, offering insights into why the monumental complex was built.

Reading Borough Council's proposed parking scheme aimed at easing pressures around a hospital is faced with opposition from hospital staff, residents, and a local resident, who argue it will exacerbate parking issues, be particularly problematic for hospital staff and patients, and potentiallymake living in the area difficult. The council, however, claims it has consulted with the public for up to five years on prioritizing parking for residents in the area and is seeking further public input.

U.S. Navy Petty Officer Aimee Mejia, 21, was involved in a three-car accident on Okinawa, injuring two people due to driving under the influence, which is several times the legal limit. This is the latest incident sparking ongoing local protest against U.S. military presence, escalating tensions as restrictions on U.S. personnel's off-base activities are strengthened, with the Navy suspending alcohol consumption and tightening training protocols.

In a record-breaking tri-series, the Lions (England Lions), coached by former England captain, Andy Flower, displayed exceptional batting form with multiple players scoring more than 150 runs each. Notably, Sam Billings, Dawid Malan, and Harry Duckett showcased impressive performances, with Duckett's 220 not out being the ninth-highest List A score. Flower highlighted these young players as potentially capable of playing international cricket, and praised Duckett as a "very talented young man" with a promising international future.

Colombia and FARC rebels have agreed to continue peace talks in Havana following the release of three hostages, with a focus on de-escalating the conflict and addressing victim-family concerns. The negotiations, which began in 2012, aim to end five decades of conflict that has claimed around 220,000 lives. The next round of talks is slated for 10-17 December, with a possible resumption around mid-January.

The Save Oxfordshire Children's Centres Campaign, led by Jill Huish, held a "baby blockade" protest against Oxfordshire County Council's proposal to close 44 out of 48 children's centers and replace them with eight children and family centers to save £8m. The protest drew more than 500 people, including a call for Prime Minister David Cameron to join, as he expressed disappointment with the cuts earlier. The council maintains that it will support vulnerable families, while the government maintains that there is scope for savings across local government.

A sandcastle depicting a dead murder victim surrounded by police tape, created by Devon and Cornwall Police during a beach games competition, sparked controversy for its poor taste, offensive imagery, and trivialization of serious matters, particularly regarding sex crimes, with councillor Hannah Toms criticizing it as unsuitable for a family event. The force later apologized for any offense caused.

The new owner of Leyton Orient has taken control of the club, and manager Justin Slade anticipates changes to the club's structure, seeking support from the owner and sporting director to strengthen the squad, with the goal to improve upon their performance in the current season and hopefully gain promotion.

Tom Hatton, a 24-year-old golfer from Buckinghamshire, secured a spot at The Open Championship, USPGA at Baltusrol, and achieved his best European Tour finish of outright second with a prize payday of over €429,000, despite missing birdie chances on the back nine at the Scottish Open, where he also won £150,000 more due to a crucial putt on the final green. His main goal at Royal Troon is to make it through the weekend.

The 10-year-old Irish-bred horse, Many Clouds, suffered a rare severe pulmonary haemorrhage and collapsed after winning the Cotswold Chase at Cheltenham's Festival Trials Day, despite no significant underlying health issues, leaving the racing community determined to better understand this illness.

The12-year-old witness testified in Sheffield Crown Court that she was abused by Basharat Hussain and other men, and later forced into prostitution in Blackpool, while being taken out for a meal by Hussain and others initially. Seven individuals, including Basharat Hussain, Arshid Hussain, Qurban Ali, Majid Bostan, Sajid Bostan, Karen MacGregor, and Shelley Davies, are on trial over alleged child abuse in Rotherham, with the accused facing charges ranging from indecent assault to rape.

A 32-year-old racing cyclist, Franck Petricola, sadly passed away in an accident during the practice week of the TT race in the Isle of Man, making him the 141st fatality at the races since their inception in 1907. Despite suffering severe injuries in a crash at the North West 200 in 2014, he showed remarkable determination to make a full recovery and competed in this year's event just last month. The racing community has expressed deep sympathy for his family and friends, with an investigation into the accident now underway.

Despite a much-anticipated return of Guy Martin to the Isle of Man TT, his participation has been cancelled due to a crash he sustained during the June event and mechanical issues with the Honda machine this season. The event is looking forward to the highly competitive performances of Peter Hickman, Michael Dunlop, Dean Harrison, and potential dark horses at the world's fastest road race.

President Barack Obama has declared Louisiana a disaster area due to devastating floods, which have left over 20,000 people rescued and tens of thousands displaced in Baton Rouge, with many still trapped in their homes. Rivers in Louisiana and Mississippi are overflowing, causing widespread destruction. The flood of 2016 is being called "epic" and could rival the devastation of Hurricane Katrina in 2005.

The concussion lawsuit against the federation by parents has been resolved, with US Soccer introducing new safety measures, including limiting the amount of heading for children aged 11-13, modifying substitution rules related to concussions, and urging compliance with these changes. Meanwhile, the Football Association in England has also announced upcoming guidelines to manage suspected head injuries in football, with a focus on identifying research questions regarding long-term effects of head injury or repeated concussion episodes on the brain.

Former presidential campaign deputy director Jerome Lavrilleux stated that Nicholas Sarkozy, Jean-Francois Cope, and Batien Millot were not aware of irregularities involving fake invoices worth nearly $15m during Sarkozy's 2012 campaign, which could potentially damage the UMP party and his chances of re-election.

The Council of Mortgage Lenders reported a decrease in home repossessions (2,500) from April to June 2021, compared to the previous quarter and the same quarter in 2020. This decline is attributed to low interest rates. However, lenders encourage homeowners to prepare for future interest rate increases. The number of homeowners in arrears also fell, but the number of evicted tenants rose by 4%. Shelter suggests that rising rents and welfare cuts are causing homelessness among families.

From October to March, the city accepted 105 Syrian refugees as part of the UK's expanded resettlement programme, with Coventry taking a higher number relative to other areas, which was criticized by UKIP's James Carver for its potential strain on local services. The Government has pledged to resettle 20,000 Syrian refugees by 2020 under its Syrian Vulnerable Persons Resettlement Scheme, and 1,602 Syrians have been settled in 71 local authorities since October, with 159 in the West Midlands, 44 in Birmingham, and 10 in Stafford. Despite the controversy, Coventry City Council continues to support the resettlement of refugees based on their medical needs and involvement in the conflict in Syria.

Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff asserts that the 2016 Rio Olympics will bring honor and pride to the country, with the Olympic torch relay kicking off in May 2016 in Brasilia, traveling through 300 cities in 90-100 days, before ending at Rio's Maracana stadium at the Olympics' opening ceremony. Rousseff promises the event will be secure and successful, addressing concerns about delays, pollution, and health risks.

Italian Prime Minister Matteo Renzi's legislative package, which received final approval in the lower house of parliament, includes a reform ensuring a majority of seats to the party winning the most votes in elections. The measure aims to mitigate Italy's post-war era of unstable governments by establishing a system that awards 340 out of 630 seats to parties securing more than 40% of the national vote and triggers a second-round run-off if no party meets the threshold. Opposition parties criticized the reform for giving too much power to single parties and denying voters direct representation, leading to their boycott of the vote. Additionally, Renzi is seeking to further transform the Italian system by abolishing the Senate.

The 20-year-old football player Abdelhak Nouri, while playing for Ajax against Werder Bremen, experienced cardiac arrhythmias, and post-evaluation suggests he is unlikely to recover due to brain damage caused by a lack of oxygen supply.

Swansea, having lost six straight games, secured an important victory at Villa Park, with Andre Ayew scoring a late winner after Jordan Ayew had started the scoring for Villa, and Gylfi Sigurdsson scoring the equalizer from a free-kick. Sigurdsson believes the win will boost team morale ahead of their match against Arsenal at home, as they push to meet their pre-season targets. This win also led to the sacking of Aston Villa's manager, Tim Sherwood.

A Polish mother named Leyla Dad, using the middle name Paulina, is searching for her son Mani Dad, believed to be in the UK with his British father Zayn Dean, and is pleading with Costa coffee shop employees and customers to help find him, as he frequently visited these establishans when the family lived in England. The family had previously resided in Kettering, Northamptonshire, and Bedford before moving to Poland. Leyla launched family court proceedings to locate her son and has asked anyone with information to contact the police.

Dual citizens of Iran, Iraq, Syria, and Sudan, including a BBC presenter, are facing travel restrictions to the US under new visa rules, which they deem unfair due to ambiguity in implementation advice and potential impact on families. The rules were implemented following increased security concerns post Paris attacks, drawing criticism from European diplomats.

Sky is working to increase capacity at telephone exchanges in areas facing capacity issues, coinciding with the launch of Sky Go Extra, a service that allows offline viewing of movies and TV shows, potentially adding to network strain, especially for customers with slow internet speeds. Some users have complained about slowed download speeds below the necessary 2 megabits per second for Sky's other streaming services, impacting a small number of exchanges, primarily in Doncaster, North Wales, and Bristol, affecting less than 5% of Sky's broadband customer base. The issue is related to increased network traffic and new customer additions, with less aggressive data caps promoting a higher data usage compared to the average UK broadband user.

Joseph McHale, Kevin Schruyers, and Robin Vaughan, residents of Liverpool, were guilty of a string of ATM thefts and attempted thefts in various Scottish locations between August and November 2013 using oxygen and acetylene. They were convicted of blowing up cash machines in Aberdeen, New Deer, and other locations and stealing significant amounts of money. The investigation uncovered their activities due to Scottish banknotes being found in the Mersey area with telltale signs of dye. A Scottish resident, Francis Clark, had inadvertently provided them with a hideout after being approached at a party. Sentencing was deferred until next month at the High Court at Livingston.

Scottish Prison Service will implement mobile phone signal interference technology in two pilot prisons (HMP Shotts and Glenochil) to prevent prisoners from using contraband phones, following legislation allowing such interference. This move aims to address the problems of drug supply, organized crime, and harassment linked to mobile phone use in prisons. The technology is scheduled to be operational within weeks.

French President Francois Hollande participated in a ceremony at a former Nazi camp in Alsace to commemorate the 70th anniversary of its liberation, where he highlighted the importance of knowledge as a means of preventing future atrocities, while the ongoing surge of attacks on Jews and Muslims in France has reignited debate about social tensions, and similar commemorative events took place in Germany, Israel, and Croatia for other liberated Nazi camps, including Bergen-Belsen and Jasenovac.

Actor Johnny Depp, 52, and his wife Amber Heard, 30, are divorcing due to irreconcilable differences, with Heard filing in Los Angeles Superior Court. Recent legal issues arose when Heard illegally brought two dogs into Australia, leading to a months-long feud with Australia's Deputy PM Barnaby Joyce. The divorce coincides with Depp's mother's death and the release of his latest film, Alice Through the Looking Glass.

A container ship, Maersk Tigris, with 24 crew members, mostly from Eastern Europe and Asia, remains boarded off Bandar Abbas, Iran, after being seized by Iranian authorities on suspicion of debt-related issues from a private Iranian company. The ship, under charter from Singapore-based Rickmers Shipmanagement, was carrying commercial goods and not military equipment, and reported a distress call while navigating through waters under international agreement open to foreign ships. The U.S. Navy dispatched a destroyer and a reconnaissance plane to monitor the situation, with a Pentagon spokesman calling the actions of the Iranian Revolutionary Guards Navy patrol vessels, who ordered the ship to go deeper into Iranian waters then fired warning shots, as "inappropriate."

A request to disclose the full investigation report on the 2012 suicide of 14-year-old foster child Seren Bernard in Pembrokeshire was denied by the council, leaving the girl's mother feeling frustrated and seeking further action due to unanswered questions and concerns about public interest and transparency.

In a disappointing performance, Salford lost to Leigh, securing their place at the bottom of the Super League for the 2021 regular season, while a third-place finish for Salford, their highest league placing in 40 years, slipped away due to a series of losses in the latter part of the season. Leigh demonstrated strong performance across game management, defense, and lead changes, with key contributions from Gregg McNally, Samisoni Langi, and Josh Drinkwater, while Salford struggled with physicality and intensity.

Paul Allen, aided by Burt Rutan and Elon Musk, is developing a giant aircraft, Stratolaunch Systems, to launch unmanned rockets into orbit from high-flying aircraft, with plans for manned missions and satellite delivery; the first test flights are scheduled for 2016, following a decade of preliminary designs.

Despite Lancashire establishing a significant 264-run lead in the match thanks to Alex Davies' impressive 89, Derbyshire manage to dismiss their openers, ending the day on 27-2 at the mercy of Lancashire's bowlers, with Peter Siddle and Tom Bailey claiming the wickets, as Davies and Jarvis had earlier contributed a valuable 160-run partnership during Lancashire's innings.

Jon Stewart, known as a prominent American satirist and host of The Daily Show on Comedy Central, bid farewell to the program after 16 years, with notable guests such as Bruce Springsteen, US Secretary of State John Kerry, and Senator John McCain. He will be replaced by South African comedian Trevor Noah. The show, often regarded as a significant news source for young Americans, launched several comedian careers, including that of Stephen Colbert who replaced David Letterman on The Late Show. Famous fans and admirers marked Stewart's departure on Twitter using the hashtag #JonVoyage.

Forest, a four-time cup winner looking to return to European competition, will start their campaign in the third round against League Two side Doncaster, while their first-choice goalkeeper Dorus de Vries is expected to be out for a few weeks due to an injury he sustained in the season opener.

The Arches nightclub has gone into administration following a midnight closing time restriction due to drug abuse and disorder issues, potentially affecting 130 jobs. The Scottish Government, Creative Scotland, Glasgow Life, and Glasgow City Council are exploring options to safeguard the cultural venue's future.

A 77-year-old, Ivor Bell, a former senior Provisional IRA leader, was arrested in connection with the abduction, murder, and secret burial of Jean McConville, one of the "Disappeared" in Northern Ireland during the Troubles, and is expected to appear in court on charges of aiding and abetting murder and IRA membership.

Wigan Warriors overcame a 12-man disadvantage following a red card to Ben Flower and scored 21 unanswered points to secure victory against Warrington Wolves, boosting their confidence for the remaining season. However, with their hopes of clinching the League Leaders' Shield slim, they will aim for a home semi-final by winning their upcoming game against Catalans Dragons.

The Yorkshire Sculpture Park experienced a 170% increase in visitor numbers in September, with 100,000 people visiting to see the poppy installation; expecting its highest visitor numbers ever, with over half a million visitors, and the poppy installation creating a calm and contemplative experience for many.

The A361 between East Lyng and Burrowbridge, which was closed due to a severe flood warning, had a warning removed on 10 March, and reopened at 17:00 GMT with temporary traffic lights in place to ensure safety. The road was cleared of debris since Monday, including 30 tonnes of used sandbags and the removal of fallen trees. The A372 Langport Road will remain closed next week for the removal of flood pumps, with the Environment Agency beginning removal of pumps on Monday. The road will remain closed after the pumps have been removed for a flood damage assessment and emergency repair works.

A newly discovered object, V774104, observed by Japan's Subaru telescope, is estimated to be approximately 500-1,000 km across and currently about three times further from the Sun than Pluto, making it the most distant known solar system object as of now. Scientists, including Scott Sheppard and Chad Trujillo, are examining its orbit to determine whether it follows an inward or outward trajectory, comparable to objects like Eris, 2012 VP113, and Sedna. The team specializes in detecting solar system outliers, and the object's potential origins range from being perturbed by a passing planet to being stolen from a star in the same "nursery" as the Sun.

Ashley Yates, a former head teacher at The Tynings Primary School in Staple Hill, South Gloucestershire, has admitted charges of making indecent images of children and voyeurism. The crime involved filming several students and staff members using a spy pen, and further adult victims have been identified as part of the ongoing police investigation. The school is cooperating with authorities and has assured parents it will disclose information as possible without prejudicing legal proceedings. Yates is currently in custody and will appear in court again on August 9.

Great Britain's rowing team, consisting of Helena Glover and Heather Stanning, dominated the Women's Pair event in the Rio Olympics, winning gold with a 1.2 second lead over New Zealand, setting a new record of 39 consecutive races without loss. Their victory exceeded the emotional joy they felt at the London Games and placed them as double Olympic champions.

Steve and Ola, participants on Strictly Come Dancing, have faced unfounded bullying allegations in the media. Despite the negative attention, they have chosen not to engage with the claims and instead have focused on their performances, maintaining their unity as a team. They emphasized that such accusations were not a true reflection of their experience on the show and reminded viewers to consider the source of such reports before forming judgments. They also referred readers to resources offering help for those affected by bullying.

The article reports that inflation dropped to 2.6% in June from 2.9%, leading to a decline in the value of the pound against both the U.S. dollar and the euro. The drop in inflation lowered expectations for an immediate interest rate hike, but it may not completely rule out a rate hike later in the year if economic conditions improve. The FTSE 100 initially rose due to the weaker pound but ended the day down 13.91 points, while Royal Mail shares increased due to a 1% rise in revenues.

Actress Vicky McClure, who has a tram in Nottingham named after her, experienced a misunderstanding in 2015 when a conductor asked for her ticket, despite her and her mother being offered a free ride after the tram was named in her honor.

The inquest into the death of 14-year-old Alice Gross, who was found dead in the River Brent in west London in September 2014, will examine if government and police failures contributed to her death and whether the systems for monitoring foreign offenders are robust. Alice's mother, Rosalind Hodgkiss, expressed concerns about the lack of monitoring of foreign national Arnis Zalkalns, a convicted murderer who was the prime suspect in Alice's death but died before being charged. Zalkalns was also the suspect in his own wife's murder.

The Local Data Company and the University of Stirling's research shows that Scotland's average retail vacancy rate decreased from 14.5% to 13.7%, with East Kilbride having the highest vacancy rate and Inverurie the lowest. Nearly 40% of empty stores have been vacant for more than three years, and town vacancy rates improved at twice the rate of cities. The report highlights the growing significance of leisure businesses in towns and cities, with Aberdeen having the highest proportion of charity shops in a city, and Penicuik in Midlothian having the greatest proportion of charity shops in a town. Matthew Hopkinson of the Local Data Company notes the chronic vacancy issue, suggesting it could stifle the growth of healthy and sustainable communities.

Rory McWhirter fraudulently obtained personal details from individuals for fake job applications, securing their marriage certificates to falsely register births, and ultimately claimed over £34,000 in welfare benefits based on these fake births. His elaborate scheme was foiled when he was recognized at an Aberdeen registry office. Despite earning £80,000 per year, his solicitor argued for leniency due to previous business failures and lack of funding from family. However, the court found his actions to be a "sophisticated fraudulent scheme" attacking multiple systems, and sentenced McWhirter to prison.

The authorities are attempting to demolish Awamiya's old quarter, a predominantly Shia area in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia, causing violence, displacement, and accusations of human rights abuses against the Shia population who claim marginalization and discrimination by the Sunni monarchy. The unrest escalated following the execution of Shia cleric Nimr al-Nimr in 2016, and the disputed executions and bombings in the region since then.

The article discusses the frustrations of young people in Belfast, aged 16 to 18, who are struggling to find employment despite having completed their education. They criticize the current political climate in Northern Ireland, where they perceive the politicians as being more focused on personal gain during election times and less concerned about addressing issues such as job opportunities, drug reform, and better health care when not campaigning.

Barnet Council's Chief Executive, Andrew Travers, resigned following election polling errors that caused voter disenfranchisement and begged for their votes. An independent investigation into the issue, focusing on the EU Referendum arrangements, has been initiated.

Manager Neil Warnock has extended a patient offer for the midfielder Peter Whittingham to decide on a new deal, giving him ample time to consider the proposition, which he has been celebrated as a ten-year club veteran, while Emyr Huws and Stuart O'Keefe are not part of Warnock's long-term plans.

A BBC and BuzzFeed News investigation revealed suspected match-fixing in elite tennis, with tennis player Andy Fleming advocating severe consequences for any proven offenders and expressing frustration over the difficulty of proving match-fixing, while assuring participants in the Australian Open that the matches are pure and fair.

A 60-year-old man, suspected of producing a firearm but without making threats or demands, surrendered to police after holding a female staff member hostage in a bank interview room on Bristol Road South, Northfield. No customers were harmed during the incident.

A British computer software programmer named Mohammed Ali, from Liverpool, is on trial at the Old Bailey for attempting to illegally possess a lethal quantity of ricin, a deadly toxin, after ordering it online using an alias, unknowingly interacting with an undercover FBI agent. Despite showing signs of Asperger's syndrome, he has denied the charge and claimed his actions were motivated by the television series Breaking Bad, pushing the boundaries of technology.

Newport County is facing criticism over the condition of Rodney Parade's pitch from rugby union team Newport Gwent Dragons, as the County has reportedly incurred additional costs for drainage work on the field, making it more expensive to maintain than what the club pays annually.

Approximately 69% of the surveyed individuals admitted to working while unwell, primarily due to fear of accumulating work, while 23% falsely claimed sick days. The report suggests this practice, known as presenteeism, can be detrimental to business performance due to lower productivity and morale.

The British pound declined against both the US dollar and the euro, while the FTSE 100 index closed marginally up, driven by mining shares. Notable falls included Hikma, down 8.2%, due to regulatory delays for a new drug, Centrica, down 5.4%, due to concerns over regulation and potential price wars, and BT, down 4.5%, following a drop in annual profits.

Russian hacker Roman Seleznev, son of a Russian MP, was found guilty of stealing nearly 3 million credit card numbers from US pizza chains in Washington state over six years, with 3,700 businesses affected. He faces a four-year mandatory prison sentence following the trial, with plans for an appeal against his conviction on grounds of an illegal arrest and misuse of evidence. The US authorities maintain that Seleznev was prosecuted for his actions, not his nationality, in response to Russia's complaints about his extradition.

The individual stated that he does not possess any recordings as suggested in a tweet following his firing of James Comey, who was leading an investigation into alleged Russian interference in the election. Trump's tweet hinted at the possibility of tapes of their conversations, but Comey expressed hope that there were tapes when testifying about Trump's alleged request to drop an investigation and a request for loyalty.

Liberty, led by Sanjeev Gupta, plans to submit a letter of intent for a bid to acquire Tata Steel's assets, including the UK's largest steelworks in Port Talbot, on Tuesday. The firm has gathered a team of advisers, including Macquarie, and its focus is on recycling scrap metal rather than traditional blast furnace methods, having previously acquired several steel plants in the UK. A management buyout team, Excalibur Steel UK Limited, is also planning to submit a bid. The UK government has pledged to support a buyer by investing up to 25% in a new business and providing hundreds of millions in finance. Tata Steel has been losing £1m per day and has not publicly set a deadline for a deal.

The 19 councils in the Nottingham region are prioritizing the extension of the tram system to East Midlands Airport, the proposed HS2 station at Toton, and potential links to Derby and other cities in devolution negotiations, with cost and timetable details yet to be determined.

The five-time world champion, Ronnie O'Sullivan, won the Masters tournament with a record-tying 9-0 victory, attributing his success to modifying his game and emphasizing the importance of mental focus, stating that even without his best form, he can still win provided he remains mentally focused.

The devastating weekend storms in Poland resulted in six fatalities, extensive property damage, and the felling of over eight million cubic meters of lumber across 45,000 hectares of forest, particularly affecting areas like Torun, Gdansk, and Poznan. The incident is said to be the worst forest disaster in Polish (and possibly European) history. The disaster occurs as the Polish government faces criticism for logging in Europe's oldest forest, Bialowieza, a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its rare wildlife, with oppositions including Unesco, EU officials, and green activists. The European Court of Justice will decide if the logging ban should remain, as the Polish government argues it is necessary to protect the forest from bark beetle infestation, and faces potential multimillion euro fines if they lose the case.

Singer Enrique Iglesias was injured at a concert in Tijuana, Mexico when he reached for a drone camera taking photos of the audience, requiring reconstructive surgery and subsequent recovery for several weeks before resuming his tour on July 3 in Mexico City.

In the Super League match between Leeds Rhinos and Warrington Wolves, Matt Parcell scored a hat-trick, Joel Moon scored his 15th try in 16 games, and Jamie Jones-Buchanan also scored as Leeds Rhinos beat Warrington Wolves 26-0, keeping the Wire scoreless. Leeds moved up to third place with their fifth win in seven games.

William (Plum) Smith, who spent a decade in prison for a 1972 shooting and played a crucial role in the 1994 ceasefire of loyalist paramilitary groups, was remembered for his significant contributions to peace efforts and his negotiations with traditional enemies, as highlighted by Martin McGuinness and Brian Ervine.

Olive Cooke, a 92-year-old Bristol resident and long-standing Royal British Legion (RBL) poppy seller, has been promoting the remembrance of World War I and II heroes for over 75 years, particularly highlighting the sacrifice of her late husband, Leslie Hussey-Yeo, who was killed in action in 1943. The RBL categorizes Mrs. Cooke as their "most-valued poppy collector" for her past 12 years of service, primarily selling poppies at the entrance of Bristol Cathedral.

Shimon Peres, a prominent Israeli statesman and peace activist, former Prime Minister and President, who played a crucial role in Israel's founding, won the Nobel Peace Prize, and advocated for peace with the Palestinians, died after suffering a stroke two weeks prior.

A major survey at Queen's University, involving a large portion of the staff, reveals low ratings for leadership and change management, but high levels of personal pride, work interest, and overall positive sentiments. The university acknowledges the results and plans to collaborate with staff to address pain points and develop action plans for improvement.

The X-47B jet, a tailless, stealthy unmanned aircraft developed by Northrop Grumman for the US Navy, successfully completed its maiden flight, marking a significant step towards a new era of high-speed, radar-evading drones; scheduled for further testing in 2013, before potential use from an aircraft carrier.

Airbus has reduced the planned deliveries of its double-decker A380 planes due to low demand and is hoping for increased orders with an upgraded version, while also grappling with engine reliability issues on its A320neo aircraft and discussing possibilities for future deliveries of the A350 planes with Qatar Airways.

Nearly 40% of coral at the Dongsha Atoll in the South China Sea died during the 2015/16 El Nino event, according to experts, which emphasizes the need for drastic global warming reduction to preserve coral reefs worldwide, particularly those in shallow water regions.

Researchers at the University of Queensland and Monash University have discovered a protein found in the venom of Australian funnel-web spiders named Hi1a, which has shown significant potential in preventing brain damage in lab rats after a stroke. They observed that Hi1a blocked acid-sensing ion channels within the brain, a key driver of brain damage after a stroke, and thus exhibited "great promise" as a future stroke treatment. The research is still in its early stages and has yet to undergo human trials.

Oldham took an early lead against Bradford City through a Peter Clarke header, but Bradford dominated most of the game, with multiple chances, only to draw level via a penalty scored by Billy Clarke after a foul by Ousmane Fane. Despite Bradford's possession and numerous attempts, the score remained 1-1 at full-time.

Experts have expressed cautious optimism for the drug aducanumab, which showed promise in halting memory decline and reducing amyloid plaques in a small study, but concern remains due to side effects and past failures in Alzheimer's drug development, as larger phase 3 trials with 2,700 patients are now underway.

Lowly Oldham Roughyeds pulled off a stunning upset in the Challenge Cup, defeating Super League side Hull KR 24-28, with star player Richard Lepori scoring two tries. The result was particularly significant for Oldham, who are in their first season in the second tier of the championship, while Hull KR, who are one of the top tiers, have struggled this season with only two wins in Super League. After the match, Hull KR coach James Webster described his team's performance as an "utter embarrassment," while Oldham's coach Scott Naylor hailed it as one of the biggest wins in the club's history.

The BBC's director general, Tony Hall, has outlined a strategy for the corporation's future, aiming to become an "open BBC for the internet age," with plans for a children's iPlayer, local reporters sharing work with local newspapers, an Ideas Service platform, and a focus on quality drama. However, due to anticipated funding cuts, the BBC will need to shut down or downsize some services, without specifying which areas might be affected. The plan is about partnership rather than competition, seeking to work with cultural bodies and companies like Netflix and Amazon in a global marketplace. Some concerns have been raised about partnerships with newspapers and local news provision.

The Equality and Human Rights Commission has written to political leaders expressing concern over an increase in hate attacks since the UK's EU referendum, including racist, anti-Semitic, and homophobic attacks. The commission calls for "accurate information and respectful debate," and urges politicians to recognize and address the widening divisions in society. The letter also criticizes government policies that may contribute to these tensions, such as the proposed plan to require companies to disclose the proportion of foreign workers they employ. The commission suggests a review of sentences for hate crimes and calls for more concerted action to address the issue.

Ms. Evans, formerly a UKIP policy maker and the author of their 2015 general election manifesto, is suspended from the party and cannot run for leadership due to a handful of individuals at the top who prevented her from doing so, as she wished. She has voiced support for councillor Lisa Duffy to succeed Nigel Farage and has called for UKIP to break free of its hard-right image, conduct internal reforms, and become a popular, consensual political party.

In England, a new grading system will replace traditional letters with numbers (1-9), and coursework will be eliminated for most subjects starting with students taking GCSEs in 2017. The changes in curriculum and assessment format are intended to improve core skills in maths and English, with a focus on deep learning, grammar, spelling, and punctuation. The reforms are scheduled to begin in autumn 2015 for English language, English literature, and maths, with other subjects being revised over the following year. Similar changes are being considered in Wales, but Northern Ireland and Scotland are not making any changes to their existing examination systems.

Retired Gen. David Petraeus, who served under Presidents Bush and Obama and faced a scandal regarding classified material, indicated a willingness to serve under Trump if asked and suggested that Trump's potential outreach to Russia could be comparable to Nixon's overtures to China.

Supporters of newly elected President Mohammed Mursi are in a standoff with military generals who have been ruling Egypt since President Hosni Mubarak's ousting. Hillary Clinton met with Mursi and urged compromise, praising Egypt's military council for their interim leadership. The U.S. is slowly learning to engage with the Muslim Brotherhood, who were previously shunned, and empathizing that they need each other. The meeting addressed efforts to stabilize Egypt's democracy and alliances, particularly addressing the reinstatement of a parliament and maintaining peace with Israel.

The article discusses Derek Bruder's testimony during the inquests into the Hillsborough disaster, where he recounted being visited by a police officer, Matthew Sawers, in 1990. Bruder was asked to revise his initial statement due to pressure from a pathologist about a teenager named Kevin Williams, though Sawers denies applying pressure to change the statement's meaning. Bruder maintains that West Midlands Police intentionally manipulated his original statement. The inquests are ongoing.

The article discusses how Oh Wonder, an anonymous band for almost a year, wrote their upbeat and energetic new album "Ultralife" after a chance encounter with a bloodied stranger on a train, which inspired a song called "High on Humans" about the power of human connection. The album, set for release in July, was inspired by a successful two-year online music phenomenon, a unique vocal style, and the desire to write about the human experience in this day and age. The band values their anonymity but acknowledges it might be compromised as their fame grows.

In a Premier League clash, Chelsea's Bertrand Traore capitalized on a Nemanja Matic pass to open the scoring, but Stoke City responded when Mame Biram Diouf headed in Xherdan Shaqiri's cross. The Potters' Bojan came close to winning it in injury time, but Thibaut Courtois thwarted him. Both teams remain distant from the Champions League spots.

William C Campbell, Satoshi Omura, and Youyou Tu's research has led to the development of life-changing drugs (ivermectin, artemisinin) to combat diseases like malaria, river blindness (onchocerciasis), and elephantiasis (lympatic filariasis), affecting over 3.4 billion people globally. These treatments are the result of discoveries originating from bacteria found in a Japanese golf course, traditional Chinese medicine, and ancient literature.

The article discusses the Nelson Mandela Foundation's criticism of South African President Zuma for allegedly allowing corruption and misuse of state resources, causing a threat to the country's democracy. The Foundation is urging the African National Congress to take action to restore the government, as investigations into Zuma's dealings with the Gupta family continue, leading to possible impeachment or corruption trial proceedings.

British comedian and actress Miranda did a gallop during the curtain call at the opening night of Annie, a West End musical at London's Piccadilly Theatre, where she stars as the unconventional orphanage owner, Miss Hannigan, outside of her normal plummy-pleasant roles. The performance received mostly positive reviews, with The Telegraph praising her for taking her out of her comfort zone, while The Guardian was less convinced, stating that it's difficult to accept her as an accomplice to the character's wrongdoings due to her excessive humor. The child actors and the scene-stealing Labradoodle, Amber, playing Annie's dog Sandy, have shared the lead roles, and the production includes classic songs such as "It's a Hard Knock Life," "Tomorrow," and "Easy Street." The theatre community believes that musicals like Annie provide much-needed optimism in the wake of recent terrorist attacks. Annie runs at the Piccadilly Theatre until 6 January 2018.

In this article, it is reported that Georginio Wijnaldum scored two goals, one each assisted by Mikel Merino and Shelvey, as Newcastle United secured a 2-1 victory over West Ham United, climbing out of the relegation zone. Steve McClaren was commended for his team's performance, while West Ham's manager Slaven Bilic acknowledged their early deficit and lamented missed opportunities.

Major supermarkets in the UK broke tradition by reducing diesel prices below petrol levels for the first time since 2001, with Morrisons leading the price cut. The shift is attributed to cheaper wholesale diesel costs and increased supply from refineries outside the UK, potentially resulting in diesel prices lower by up to 4p per litre compared to petrol over the next fortnight, according to RAC fuel spokesman Simon Williams. The change is significant as petrol prices have typically observed more sluggish decreases compared to diesel.

The UN General Assembly's 70th gathering in New York is a crucial platform for African leaders, providing diplomatic immunity and opportunities for international engagement, despite commonly associated issues like corruption and shopping sprees. Africa's relationship with the UN is complex and fractured, but necessary due to ongoing conflicts, humanitarian crises, and issues like hunger and economic instability. The UN plays a significant role in peacekeeping efforts, yet faces controversies such as allegations of mineral exploitation and sexual abuse by peacekeepers. The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) have been agreed upon, with ending hunger as a prime focus, as food security remains a pressing concern in Africa due to environmental factors and economic instability in countries like Malawi. The UN serves as a critical lifeline for many vulnerable individuals and communities across the continent.

Superman-logo pills containing the harmful drug PMMA may still be in circulation, warns the police, with Dr Adam Winstock suggesting the pills may have originated from the Netherlands and are often mistaken for MDMA. He advises staying hydrated, monitoring friends' safety, using home testing kits cautiously, and seeking immediate medical attention if unsure about a drug's effects.

Mr Banks, the Leave.EU campaign chairman, has urged UKIP's current leader Paul Nuttall to re-engage ex-leader Nigel Farage as a key asset and to implement a new strategy to become more relevant and electable, ousting a faction of allegedly unhelpful senior figures and appointing a CEO from industry to lead a membership drive and target seats. In response, UKIP's MEP Patrick O'Flynn emphasized the importance of donors not dictating party affairs.

The article describes a service called Invisible Girlfriend/Boyfriend that allows users to buy a facade of a romantic relationship, complete with text messages, voicemails, and even a backstory. Users pay $15-$25 a month for this service, often to maintain personal or social situations, such as getting parents off their back or making an ex-jealous. The service is popular, with over 60% of users opting for boyfriend accounts, and is seen by some as a source of companionship rather than a sad or pathetic choice.

Germany displayed a dominant offensive performance in a 2-0 victory over Poland, with Thomas Muller, Karim Bellarabi, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and Mario Gotze standout contributors. However, they showed minor vulnerabilities in defence, which Scotland may exploit in their upcoming match.

In the championship, an equalizer by Sam Gallagher in the final minutes denied Bristol City a third successive win as they remain four points above the relegation zone, while Rovers are still two points from safety, with three games remaining; both teams missed chances throughout the game, with on-loan Chelsea striker Tammy Abraham having the best opportunity but striking straight at the goalkeeper.

Scotland aims to send off outgoing coach Gregor Townsend's successor, Vern Cotter, with a victory over Ireland in the opening Six Nations match, despite Ireland's recent success and the inexperience of their front-row players. This pursuit is inspired by the incentive offered by Cotter's departure and the rivalry with Ireland, particularly with the inclusion of South African player CJ Stander in Ireland's team.

John Guidetti scores a free-kick following Pascali's red card and a professional foul on Scepovic, Kilmarnock's goalkeeper Conor Brennan makes several impressive saves but cannot prevent Scepovic from scoring a second after the break. Kilmarnock struggle to keep up with Celtic in the second half, with Scepovic eventually getting the last laugh over Brennan.

According to a study by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), Northern Irish pupils have higher life satisfaction scores compared to their counterparts in the UK, but concerns over exam anxiety, bullying, and heavy internet usage remain issues. Northern Irish pupils have high parent-teacher engagement, academic ambition, and university expectations, but these digital practices can lead to lower life satisfaction. The study also identifies gender and socio-economic disparities in life satisfaction among students worldwide.

Crystal Palace overcame Everton 3-2 after a comeback from 1-0 down, with Romelu Lukaku's goal being the highlight of the Toffees' early dominance. Neil Warnock's men equalized with a penalty following a defensive error, took the lead within minutes of the second half, and extended it to 3-1 before Leighton Baines converted a late penalty for Everton, who nearly equalized but ultimately fell short. The result demonstrates Palace's resilience and tactical acumen under Warnock's guidance.

Freelance sports journalist Gary Carter, aged 36, was found with head injuries in Bethnal Green early on Friday morning following an altercation. His wife Gemma stated that he was heavily sedated while waiting for the swelling on his brain to subside. A 35-year-old man, James Flanagan, was charged with causing grievous bodily harm. The case is currently under investigation by Scotland Yard. Carter, who regularly works for The Sun, was in London to cover a rugby league match between England and New Zealand. His colleagues in the sport and on social media have expressed well-wishes for a speedy recovery.

British rapper Tinie Tempah, who holds the record for the most number one singles in this decade amongst British artists, discusses his second home studio, where he has been working on his third album Youth for more than two years, having taken inspiration from meeting up with his friends to reignite his creativity and connect with his roots. He reflects on his journey from Peckham's Aylesbury estate to achieving success in the music industry, and shares his admiration for the self-reliance and determination of contemporary grime artists such as Skepta and Stormzy, emphasizing their importance in mainstream British culture.

Mobile operators, led by O2, are hoping to accelerate the government's and Ofcom's process for allocating spectrum, aiming to bring 4G networks to many places as early as May or June 2013 instead of the end of the year, while expressing disappointment over the delay and the advantage previously given to EE.

The Conservative party has decided to discontinue a policy offering free school lunches to children in the first three years of primary school, instead opting for a cheaper free breakfast option. This decision has drawn criticism from teachers and unions who claim it is mean-spirited and will affect children's overall nutrition, particularly those from low-income families. The policy, initially introduced by the coalition government in 2014, has been criticized for being costly, with many schools needing to upgrade kitchen facilities before implementation. Critics argue that the decision to cancel free lunches does not make financial sense given the investment already made in school kitchens and staffing, and the unfunded costs schools are facing, such as teachers' pay, pensions, and national contributions.

A shooting incident took place at a busy downtown area of Tel Aviv, leaving four seriously injured. Israeli security forces launched a search for the gunman, who is believed to be an Israeli Arab from the north, but the motive behind the attack remains unclear. The attack took place on a Friday afternoon during the peak of the weekend and near a bar, leading to speculation about potential hate crime or links to organized crime.

Singer Dean Owens, researching his family tree, discovered his great great grandfather Ambrose Salvona was buried in Inverness. A resident offered help, and Ambrose's grave was later found, revealing he was a popular, colorful character and a lion tamer in the Highlands. The discovery inspired Owens' song "Dora," about his grandmother who grew up in Salvona's circus.

At Glastonbury 2021, sustainably-sourced recycled steel pint cups are introduced on a major scale for the first time. However, they are not compulsory and not all bars offer them. Their awkward shape and lack of a logo make them difficult to throw as missiles, unlike recyclable plastic cups. The cups are intended to be part of a reusable revolution, aiming to reduce waste and promote British steel industry. The festival organizers opted for stainless steel over plastic due to the toxic substances released during plastic glass production and the environmentally harmful nature of plastic waste.

A 15-year-old boy survived the earthquake by drinking water from wet clothes and eating clarified butter, while a woman in her 20s was rescued after being trapped for over 8 hours. The rescue effort involves teams from various countries, but relief efforts are being hampered by bad weather and difficulties reaching remote areas. Many survivors are falling ill due to contaminated water, and the death toll has risen to 6,130 with over 13,000 injured. Climbing on Mount Everest is expected to resume next week, and, despite extensive damage, the number of casualties in many villages was lower than feared due to people working outside when the quake struck.

JP Morgan plans to relocate hundreds to possibly a thousand staff members to Dublin, Frankfurt, and Luxembourg as part of contingency plans for potential post-Brexit disruptions in the EU. This move comes as several global banks prepare to relocate staff from London due to uncertainty about "passporting" rights post-Brexit.

The article states that police in Ferguson broke up a crowd after a curfew started, a police car was shot at, and a person was injured in an unrelated shooting. The shooting of 18-year-old black teenager Michael Brown by a white policeman on August 9 has sparked allegations of police brutality in the primarily black suburb of Ferguson, leading to protests and riots. The officer who shot Brown was identified as Darren Wilson, a six-year police veteran with no prior complaints. The shooting is being investigated by the US justice department and territorial authorities are working to restore peace.

Diane Abbott, the Labour shadow home secretary, criticized Theresa May for allowing a decrease in police officer numbers during May's tenure as home secretary, suggesting this contributed to the security situation leading to recent terrorist attacks. The Conservatives dismissed these views as "dangerous" and added that armed police numbers have increased.

The world champions, New Zealand, routed Wales in the final Test with a score of 46-6, marking Wales' 29th consecutive loss to the All Blacks and the heaviest loss for Wales in nine years. Warren Gatland, the Welsh coach, sees numerous lessons for his team from this defeat, aiming to improve on these learnings when they meet again. Steve Hansen, the New Zealand coach, attributes Wales' performance not to a lack of effort but to potential distractions from the long season and the World Cup year.

Five individuals, including a 17-year-old British boy named Stephen Thomas who was a talented photographer and a driving force behind the Swindon Down's Syndrome Group, died in a boat accident in Canada. The incident happened on the open, upper deck of the boat where the victims were not wearing life jackets. The Canadian government is investigating the cause of the accident, and officials suggest the rapid response from the local community saved more lives. A 27-year-old Australian man is still missing, and his girlfriend and her family were on board when the boat sank.

The article describes a signing ceremony of a ceasefire agreement by several armed groups in Myanmar (Burma), which President Thein Sein said broke new ground toward a peaceful future and federal government structure. However, key active rebel groups, including the Karen National Union, the United Wa State Army, and the Kachin Independence Organisation, did not sign the agreement, leaving questions about the deal's effectiveness and lasting political settlement.

Facebook was ordered to remove a page targeting a Northern Irish man with a history of sexual offenses from the 1980s, as it amounted to harassment and a potential violation of his human rights. The man sought an interim injunction and damages from Facebook Ireland Ltd, citing threats to his safety. While the court upheld the interim order, it emphasized that it did not suppress information about the man's criminal record already in the public domain. The judge also acknowledged the case's sensitivity and reminded that similar cases would be highly fact-dependent.

Apple is planning to launch a news app this year, inviting publishers to participate. The terms of the agreement, sent via an email, automatically presume acceptance unless active opt-out is stated. The terms require publishers to indemnify Apple for any legal issues related to RSS content, and allow Apple to place ads next to publishers' content without payment. This opt-out method is considered unusual, and some consider it presumptuous. The bid to launch with as much content as possible may lead to objections and potential legal issues.

The article discusses the concerns on the U.S. Pacific territory of Guam, home to significant U.S. military facilities, following escalating threats from North Korea. While some residents are anxious about the potential threat, Governor Eddie Baza Calvo reassures there is no immediate danger. The island's population varies in their level of worry, with some expressing concern while others remain unphased, viewing the threats as a long-standing situation. Local authorities are prepared for any events and are taking necessary precautions.

Sentinel-1b was launched into orbit by a Soyuz rocket from French Guiana as part of the European Union's flagship space project, Copernicus, which aims to monitor Earth's health and environment with a multitude of applications, including tracking shipping lanes for pollution and icebergs, and observing land surfaces for signs of subsidence. The satellite will work alongside Sentinel-1a, and along with other upcoming satellites, they will provide an avalanche of data and help with services ranging from air quality updates to infrastructure planning. Additionally, a French space agency mission called Microscope, which aims to investigate the equivalence principle, was flown on the same mission.

The article suggests that the pound has gained 1% due to the snap election call by Theresa May, implying markets believe she will win and gain a larger majority, potentially leading to a softer Brexit, thus strengthening the pound. The stock market, however, fell due to UK's large companies earning in foreign currencies, as a rising pound decreases the value of those earnings in sterling terms. Business groups generally support the election as it provides more certainty for policy, but there are concerns about potential distractions from urgent priorities. The economy has shown resilience since the referendum, with increasing average wages and record employment levels, thus creating a potential economic window for the political gamble.

A hiker named Pavlina Pizova got lost during a hike on the Routeburn track in Fiordland National Park with her partner Ondrej Petr, but due to bad conditions, they became stranded. Petr later died after a slip on an ice slope, leaving Pizova to spend a night with his body before finding shelter. She survived alone in a hut for nearly a month before being found by a search team.

Elena, a 40-year-old Muscovite, and her husband are struggling to manage their debt of over a million roubles due to banks, as they live just above poverty level and recently lost her job. Millions of Russians have loans or mortgages, with many encountering problems paying them, including those with arrears stretching back over three months. This debt crisis stems from a long history of borrowing, exacerbated by financial hardship due to the global financial crisis and Western sanctions against Russia.

The Denver court has denied media requests for expanded coverage of the James Holmes case, the suspect in the Batman movie shooting that killed 12 and injured 58, while still allowing filming of court proceedings. The court's decision followed calls from some victims' families to avoid using the suspect's name and photos. Meanwhile, the investigation at Holmes' apartment continued, with discoveries of 30 grenades, several gallons of gasoline, and a booby-trap. The shooting's aftermath also saw support efforts, such as visits from Batman star Christian Bale to victims in the hospital and a Facebook photo of Bale at the hospital being posted online. Additionally, a pregnant woman who survived the shooting gave birth to a baby boy, while her husband remains in critical condition. There are renewed calls for banning high-capacity gun magazines in the U.S., but with elections approaching, there are no immediate prospects for gun control legislation.

The Art Recovery Group, headed by Christopher Marinello, is working to combat the international art market trafficking of looted Syrian antiquities, by running the Art Claim database, checking international auction houses, online marketplaces, and aiding law enforcement worldwide, to identify and prevent the sale of such objects with no known provenance, in an effort to halt the crisis and illegal funding of terrorism groups like ISIS.

The report, following the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant disaster, found that the loss of life, contamination, and widespread damage were avoidable and a result of systemic failures. These failures included a reluctance to question authority, collusion between regulators, government, and operators, inadequate safety measures, poor emergency response, and insufficient evacuation planning. The report also highlighted the lack of accountability and unclear responsibilities of organizations involved, and emphasized that cosmetic solutions would not address the fundamental root causes of the disaster.

The article discusses the success of the UK government's auto-enrolment programme, which has seen a 95% compliance rate among small businesses, with a focus on the later stages that include enrolling more diverse workers. However, there are concerns about the adequacy of contribution levels, with the average employer contribution being 3%, and calls for increased minimum rates to ensure a decent retirement. Additionally, concerns have been raised about certain trusts managing pensions for small firms.

The article summarizes a Canadian-led study published in Nature Geoscience that estimates the total amount of water stored in the top 2km of Earth's surface, with modern groundwater (6%) being quickly renewed, sensitive to climate change, and human contamination, making it a vital resource to manage sustainably. The research also reveals significant variations in the distribution of modern groundwater reserves worldwide.

The European Challenge Cup final for 2017 will be held in Edinburgh, alongside the Champions Cup final, following a successful bid assisted by the Scottish Government and Event Scotland. This decision is a testament to Scotland's passion for rugby and its ability to host world-class events.

Edward Snowden, the former CIA worker wanted by the US for leaking details of surveillance programs, has requested temporary asylum in Russia but remains in Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport's transit zone due to unprocessed asylum application and lack of travel documents. His lawyer, Anatoly Kucherena, noted Edward's anxiousness about leaving the airport, hoping for a quick resolution. The White House expressed the need for clarity from Russia regarding Snowden's status, advocating for his extradition to face espionage charges, which Russia has refused to do.

Brazil's Attorney-General has requested the Supreme Court to initiate an investigation into former President Lula for his alleged involvement in the Operation Car Wash scandal, a multi-billion dollar kickback scheme at Petrobras, due to testimony given by a senator in a plea bargain. Evidence against Lula involves suspicious property transactions and illicit benefits including renovations and donations from construction companies involved in the scandal. The investigation could put significant pressure on President Rousseff, Lula's mentor, who is already facing impeachment proceedings.

The article summarizes that three SAS candidates, L/Cpl Craig Roberts, Cpl James Dunsby, and L/Cpl Edward Maher, died during a selection exercise in 2013 due to heat-related causes.
